findings.body:
**Enforce the deadline inside the queue drain poll.**

With 60 seconds left and six recorded runs whose probes each time out after 30 seconds, one poll takes about 180 seconds before the runbook checks its deadline. Capping the sleep between polls cannot bound that work.

Pass the remaining deadline into the controller scan. Cap each probe to the time left, and report any unobserved work as unresolved when time expires. Preserve the current fail-stop behavior.
findings.title: Enforce the deadline inside the queue drain poll.

findings.body:
**Handle interruption after creating the admission marker.**

If Ctrl-C interrupts the token flush or fsync, the marker exists but `acquired` is still false. The `OSError` handler does not catch the interrupt. `restore_before_switch` then skips cleanup, and the CLI exits 1 without reporting that admission can still be disabled.

Handle interruption during marker creation as a potentially completed claim. Remove the marker only if ownership is proven. Otherwise, report recovery required with the marker path and the evidence needed to reconcile it.
findings.title: Handle interruption after creating the admission marker.

findings.body:
**Reject a runtime entry that lost execute permission.**

If the measured entry changes from mode `0755` to `0644` after the drain, its path and digest still match. This check permits the restart. The rollback path uses the same check, so it can also restart triggers against the unusable entry.

Compare the observed mode with the pre-deploy measurement before either restart. Keep the existing placeholder handling.
findings.title: Reject a runtime entry that lost execute permission.

findings.body:
**Validate journal field types before matching their patterns.**

A JSON deploy record with `prior_head: 42` reaches `SHA_RE.match(42)`. The resulting `TypeError` bypasses the CLI handlers. A non-string, nonempty `prior_tag` has the same failure. Use the existing `_hex` and `_tag` predicates so malformed fields produce a JSON refusal and valid strings still proceed. As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed.”
findings.title: Validate journal field types before matching their patterns.

findings.body:
**Make interrupted runbook deployments block subsequent mutations.**

If the process dies during the switch, the locks disappear but the recovery evidence remains in a nested `run-*` directory. The controller scans only top-level `controller-*.json` files and does not check the admission marker before a unit transaction. If the runbook dies after releasing admission, a second runbook deployment can also miss the unfinished run.

Write an unresolved deployment intent where both entrypoints check it under the controller lock. Keep it unresolved through health and recovery. A clean deployment or verified rollback should close it; process loss should not.
findings.title: Make interrupted runbook deployments block subsequent mutations.

findings.body:
**Reject invalid health delays before changing the host.**

`--health-interval-s -1` passes parsing. If the first health observation advances, the second observation calls `time.sleep(-1)`. That turns an invalid argument into a rollback of an otherwise healthy deployment. Validate the timing arguments before constructing the run, and return the usage artifact for invalid values. Keep zero valid where it intentionally means no delay.
findings.title: Reject invalid health delays before changing the host.

findings.body:
**Keep unsupported receipt types out of the tick-health failure path.**

If the deployment's local receipt schema uses `type: "number"`, a sampled local receipt reaches `_SCHEMA_TYPES["number"]` and raises `KeyError`. The standalone health command emits no JSON. The runbook treats the same exception as a deployment failure and can roll back even though ticks are advancing.

Validate schema type names before lookup. Report an unsupported type as an invalid or unverified receipt observation, while keeping supported types on the existing validation path. As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed.”
findings.title: Keep unsupported receipt types out of the tick-health failure path.

findings.body:
**Report a completed unit rollback as a failed switch, not pending recovery.**

If target completion fails but the controller restores the prior snapshot and activation, Line 2149 writes a terminal `rolled_back` record. This line then raises `RecoveryRequired`, so the CLI returns 3 even though the unfinished-transaction guard treats the record as resolved.

Return the rollback record with exit 1 for the failed switch. Reserve exit 3 for the branch where restoration or terminal recording fails. As per coding guidelines: “Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 thrown error, 2 arg error, 3 needs-human.”
findings.title: Report a completed unit rollback as a failed switch, not pending recovery.

findings.body:
**Restore the measured live config on checkout rollback.**

A prior checkout can have a live `repair.enabled` edit that is not reproduced by Git and the overlay. The deploy journal retains only its digest. Rollback calls `switch` without `rollback_config`, so the helper verifies and renders the prior commit as a forward target. The controller then reports success without checking the restored config against the recorded digest.

Retain the exact prior config in private recovery storage and bind it to the deploy journal. Keep the applicable owner and tag checks, but use the exact-byte helper branch for restoration and verify the restored digest before recording success. For older journals without recoverable bytes, report that limitation instead of claiming exact restoration.
findings.title: Restore the measured live config on checkout rollback.
